back: (Standard price - actual price) × actual quantity (bought or used as stated). Positive = favourable.
(Standard quantity for actual output - actual quantity used) × standard price.
(Standard rate - actual rate) × actual hours paid.
(Standard hours for actual output - actual hours worked) × standard rate.
Standard direct cost of actual output - actual direct cost = material price + usage + labour rate + efficiency variances.
Actual units produced × standard quantity per unit. The yardstick for usage and efficiency variances.

front: Why price variances use the actual quantity
back: The price difference applies to everything bought or used at the actual price; the quantity effect is left to the usage variance at standard price.
Cheap, poor material may give a favourable price variance but adverse usage and efficiency variances.
Positive variance = favourable (profit up). Negative = adverse (profit down). Always label F or A.
